note: Uganda's large banks were tried for card terms: Stanbic Bank Uganda (the largest), Absa Bank Uganda, dfcu Bank and Bank of Africa Uganda; the Bank of Uganda's comparison of banks' rates and charges (1 April 2026) lists no card terms. Stanbic Bank Uganda's personal and private banking tariff guide (effective 27 March 2026), read in full: its credit card costs UGX 150,000 a year and UGX 22,600 to issue, charges 3% a month on the balance used, 3% on a domestic cash withdrawal, a UGX 30,000 late fee and a 4% currency conversion fee; the guide adds excise duty on its charges without stating the rate, so no tax is written; its table's text runs out of order, so its rows were matched by eye. dfcu Bank's tariff poster (effective 16 February 2026): its Visa Gold and Platinum credit cards in shillings cost UGX 120,000 and 200,000 a year for the primary card, charge 4% on a cash withdrawal (at least UGX 10,000), and 'Interest 42%' with no period stated; a yearly reading is likely (42% a month is no card's price), but as with Eswatini's, Tanzania's and Guinea-Bissau's cards no rate is written without its period, so dfcu's cards aren't written; the poster says every charge excludes 15% government excise duty. dfcu's late payment fee (10%, at least UGX 10,000) and over-limit fee (2%) don't say of what, so aren't written, nor is the 0.05% insurance, whose base isn't stated. Absa Bank Uganda's site lists no tariff guide (its candidate pages answered 404), and Bank of Africa Uganda's 2026-2027 tariff guide refused this client (403). Wave 4 (30 October 2026): Absa Bank Uganda's Retail Banking Tariff Guide (effective 5 February 2026) was found at the address Absa's other African banks use for theirs (its site's own links had answered 404) and read in full for its credit cards: the Infinite, Signature, Platinum and Classic cards cost UGX 400,000, 250,000, 220,000 and 100,000 a year with no joining fee, charge 1.75%, 2.7%, 3% and 3.5% a month, 6% for a cash advance (at least UGX 10,000) and a 6% scheme mark-up, written as the share added to spending in another currency, as Absa Ghana's is. Its late payment fee (10%, at least UGX 20,000) and over-limit fee (6%) don't say of what, so they aren't written; nor is the credit life insurance (0.08% a month, base not stated). The quarterly 'unutilised limit penalty' of UGX 25,000 falls only on a card whose limit goes unused, which the game doesn't track, so it isn't written. The guide adds 15% excise duty to every charge 'with the exception of loan related charges' without saying whether a card's charges are among those, so no tax is written. Equity Bank Uganda's tariff guide (effective 1 May 2026) prices no credit card; Centenary Bank's and Housing Finance Bank's sites answered a Cloudflare check, and DTB Uganda's and NCBA Uganda's didn't answer. So Uganda has two banks' cards, dfcu's still being unwritten for want of its rate's period.
